clauses.text:
Executive Order 10878
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN THE CHICAGO, ROCK
ISLAND AND PACIFIC RAILROAD
COMPANY AND OTHER CARRIERS
REPRESENTED BY THE WESTERN
CARRIERS’ CONFERENCE COMMIT­
TEE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EM­
PLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between
the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific
Railroad Company and other carriers
represented by the Western Carriers’
Conference Committee, designated in
List A- attached hereto and hereby made
a part hereof, and certain of their em­
ployees represented by the Switchmen’s
Union of North America, AFL-CIO, a
labor organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to
deprive a section of the country of es­
sential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the
authority vested in me by section 10 of
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of
three members, to be appointed by me,
to investigate this dispute. No member
of the board shall be pecuniarily or
otherwise interested in any organization
of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to
the President with respect to the dispute
within thirty days from the date of this
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this
date and for thirty days after the board
has made its report to the President, no
change, except by agreement, shall be
made by the Chicago, Rock Island and
Pacific Railroad Company or any other
carrier represented by the Western Car­
riers’ Conference Committee, or by their
employees, in the conditions out of which
the dispute arose.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 10878 is a Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency-board order with provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed the order’s identity from its heading and number, and confirmed a single-clause inventory. It has no own-terms end. The only held instrument that revokes it is EO 12553 (1986-02-25), which I read; the report date and the end of the status-quo period are disclosed spent facts, not ends. The searches chosen (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) carry no coverage warning and show no hit for this order that contradicts the ending.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Searched for an end earlier than 1986-02-25. The order’s own terms contain only the report direction and the status-quo period, which are report-relative deadlines and not ends. The Cruden number lookup in LOOKUPS.md finds this number cited only in the order’s own held texts, in the NMB report text where one is held, and in EO 12553. No held later order other than EO 12553 revokes, supersedes, amends or terminates it, and no statute held in the packet does so; an unnamed statute or order would in any case not end it (owner ruling 2026-10-21 unnamed instruments). The dossier’s conflicts and missing lists are empty or concern only a number citation without a change provision (report dated 1960-07-08 in the held NMB text; thirty days later is 1960-08-07).","independent_command_check":"No independent command survives: the board’s creation was performed when the order issued; the report direction and the status-quo period are time-limited by the order itself and by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; the order creates no standing office, delegation, rule or continuing duty that would outlast the report and the thirty-day period. Those spent commands nonetheless remained formally in the order until EO 12553, and the order is recorded as ending on revocation under the owner’s report-deadline ruling.","savings_check":"EO 12553 has no saving, exception or pending-matters language: a search of the whole held text for except, notwithstanding, nothing in, saving, pending and similar words found only incidental uses inside other orders’ subject lines. The board’s report and any agreement or later change in working conditions between the parties are accrued consequences that rest on the Railway Labor Act and the parties’ own acts, not on this order, and none keeps the order operative.","scope_check":"The whole order is covered: EO 12553 revokes listed orders \"and any amendments thereto\" with no exception, so no part of this one-paragraph order was left in force. The clause inventory is one clause (the whole order); I read the held text and confirm that it contains the creation, report and status-quo commands and nothing else operative."}
